clue.text: Chest is tender after cold

indicators.note: after places the word for tender behind the letter for cold

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to tender is to offer, as in tendering a payment

explanation.surface: A sore chest that flares up after catching a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective meaning sore, but it is the verb, to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox for valuables, a kind of chest.

clue.text: A poet may rely upon visit that is about work

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit

indicators.note: about means the letters for that is go round the work abbreviation

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A poet depends on a trip that concerns his writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Calliope is the Greek Muse of epic poetry, whom poets invoke for inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of epic verse is the source of inspiration that poets call on.

clue.text: Water jug upside down in sink for so long

indicators.note: in places the turned jug word inside the word for sink

parts.note: to sink is to fall

indicators.note: upside down, in a down entry, means the jug word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A jug turned over in the sink for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' turns EWER into REWE, which 'in' places inside FALL.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is a casual goodbye, and this word is a parting salutation.

clue.text: A bird that preys on fish before circling north

definitions.text: A bird that preys on fish

indicators.note: circling means the word for before goes around the north letter

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A raptor feeding on fish before flying round to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-tailed sea eagle catches fish, and crosswords often use this name for it.

clue.text: Skilfully holding back disorder in school meeting

indicators.note: holding means the word for skilfully wraps round the other piece

parts.note: doing something skilfully is doing it ably

indicators.note: back tells us the word for disorder is read from right to left

parts.note: a disorder or untidy state is a mess

explanation.surface: A head teacher deftly keeps a lid on unruly behaviour at morning gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MESS into SSEM, which 'holding' puts inside ABLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily gathering of pupils and staff in a school hall is called by this name.

clue.text: Circumvent a current fault

explanation.definitionFit: To bypass a usual process is the figurative sense; electrically, current taking an unintended low-resistance path is a fault.

clue.text: Tender put up for capital statue

indicators.note: put up, in a down entry, means the word for tender is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tender in the sense of painful is sore

explanation.surface: A bid raised for a statue in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The winged statue at Piccadilly Circus in London is popularly known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: London's famous Piccadilly Circus statue is commonly called by the name of the Greek love god.

clue.text: Small pet for soldier in Cornish town

indicators.note: in means the soldier is placed inside the town name

parts.note: Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall, in south-west England
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A little pet bought for a serviceman stationed in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar, a small parakeet, is a common pet bird.

clue.text: One hundred in a cathedral city, said to be poor

indicators.note: in places the two numeral letters inside the city name

parts.note: York, in northern England, is famous for its minster
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred people in a cathedral city are reckoned to be impoverished.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says 'Alas, poor Yorick' over the jester's skull, so he is 'said to be poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's line about the dead jester calls him poor, so the character is the one described that way.

clue.text: An important speaking part

parts.note: reads like a big role in a play, but means the body part in the throat that produces the voice

explanation.definitionFit: The voice box in the throat holds the vocal cords, so it is literally a part used in speaking.

clue.text: It's hardly surprising there's a lack of awe

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something is unsurprising; read literally, the words mean zero amazement.

clue.text: All of a tingle, perhaps, from such a beating

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of all of a tingle could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone left smarting all over after a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipping or flogging, especially as penance, is a beating of this kind.

clue.text: Antonio wandered in this state

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words Antonio wandered, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A man called Antonio roamed through some American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: The clergy can get a great many into church

indicators.note: into tells us the word for a great many is placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: a lot means a great many

explanation.surface: Clergymen can pack lots of worshippers into their church.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are collectively known by this term, from the clerical dress they wear.

clue.text: A girl's figure may be compact

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so a girl's gives DI'S
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred, a figure

explanation.surface: A woman's shapely figure might be called compact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' suggests body shape, but it is a number; 'compact' is short for compact disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact disc is commonly called by this shorter name, and the word compact alone can refer to it.

clue.text: Rise and dress

explanation.definitionFit: To get out of bed is the verb sense; an outfit or costume is the noun.

clue.text: Sort of officers who keep the flag flying?

explanation.definitionFit: Staff officers assist a commander; a flagpole is a staff that holds the flag aloft.

clue.text: Let priests go to remove mischievous spirits

indicators.note: remove read as re-move, moving the letters of let priests go again into a new order

explanation.surface: Get the clergy to perform an exorcism and drive out the troublesome ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' is read as move again, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are noisy, mischief-making ghosts said to throw objects about.

clue.text: Money fines can upset

indicators.note: upset means the letters of fines can are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Being fined can disrupt one's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds or monetary resources are a person's or body's money.

clue.text: The engineer officer's responsibility taken by the navigator

explanation.definitionFit: Engine parts that reduce friction are a ship engineer's concern; a navigator takes compass readings of position.

clue.text: No place for a private secretary?

definitions.text: No place for a private secretary?

parts.words: No place for a private secretary?
parts.note: a private secretary works for one person behind closed doors, so a job open to and serving everybody would not suit

explanation.definitionFit: A post in government service, held on behalf of the public, is the opposite of private employment.

clue.text: Depression that shows in your face

definitions.text: Depression that shows in your face

parts.words: Depression that shows in your face
parts.note: suggests visible gloom, but means a small hollow in the cheek or chin

explanation.definitionFit: A small natural hollow in the cheek, seen when smiling, is a slight depression in the skin.

clue.text: Fish, for example, with greens?

explanation.definitionFit: A dinner stage such as fish is one sense; a golf layout, which has putting greens, is the other.

clue.text: Smooth things out on board

parts.note: sounds like settling quarrels among a ship's crew, but describes pressing clothes on a household flat stand

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing creases out of laundry on an ironing board is the verb's everyday sense.

clue.text: Blame one laid on head of dean swift

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the word dean

explanation.surface: Censure piled on a cathedral dean, perhaps the satirist Jonathan Swift.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift was Dean of St Patrick's in Dublin, so 'dean swift' reads as a person; 'swift' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms meaning very fast.

clue.text: Equality includes one or two

indicators.note: includes means the word for equality holds the one inside it

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being equal covers one person or two.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple or brace of things means exactly two of them.

clue.text: They run well, naturally, and their rise is celebrated

indicators.note: their rise, in a down entry, means the word for celebrated is read from bottom up to give them

parts.note: celebrated in song means sung

explanation.surface: Natural runners whose ascent is cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their rise is celebrated' says the light read upwards gives SUNG; 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest are antelopes built for running across the savannah by nature.

clue.text: Attempt to form a party

explanation.definitionFit: Having a go is to have a bash; a lively social gathering is also called by this word.

clue.text: Soldier lacking papers? Very suspicious!

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
with no identification documents is NO ID

explanation.surface: A trooper found without his documents arouses deep suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irrationally distrustful of others is described with this word.

clue.text: Be able to repeat a vigorous dance

indicators.note: to repeat means the word for be able appears twice in a row

parts.note: to be able is can

explanation.surface: A dancer able to do an energetic routine twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: The high-kicking French music-hall routine is a lively, energetic dance.

clue.text: Regular lay preachers take this

parts.note: even means regular or uniform
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Ordinary lay people who give sermons attend this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay preachers' reads as non-clergy, but 'lay' is a ballad, and 'Regular' gives EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening prayer in the Anglican church is a service clergy lead.

clue.text: Revising his set subject

indicators.note: revising suggests reworking, so the letters of his set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student revising the topic he has been given.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation's topic or proposition is its main subject or argument.
